articles.title: Injustice 3 Leak Reportedly Reveals 2 Playable Characters
articles.summary: Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak. MP1st unearthed evidence to suggest the unannounced fighting game will feature both Supergirl and Batwoman on its roster of playable characters.
body: Batwoman (Kate Kane) dies in the canon Injustice comics, which suggests someone else has taken up the Batwoman mantle for Injustice 3, Kate Kane didn’t actually die, or the game retcons the events of the book. Either way, this is a superhero story we’re talking about — no-one stays dead forever.

Or, as MP1st suggests, Injustice 3 may not continue the story told in Injustice and Injustice 2, but act as a reboot that tells an entirely different story. NetherRealm’s other fighting game franchise, Mortal Kombat, has done this multiple times, so it wouldn’t be a huge surprise with Injustice since it’s been nearly a decade since Injustice 2 came out.

Publisher Warner Bros. has yet to announce another Injustice game, despite it being an open secret at this point. Given Paramount looks like it’s finally going to get the green light to complete its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros., perhaps that will provide some clarity on the company’s video game plan, which we know also include Hogwarts Legacy 2 and a new Batman game from Arkham developer Rocksteady.

MP1st unearthed evidence to suggest the unannounced fighting game will feature both Supergirl and Batwoman on its roster of playable characters.

articles.title: 23 Years Later, the Most Addictive Sci-Fi Show Ever Made Officially Blasts Onto Free Streaming
articles.summary: The show is Battlestar Galactica, Ronald D. Moore’s beloved sci-fi series that ran for four seasons from 2004 to 2009. Once Fred and Carrie start watching, they cannot stop.
body: There’s a classic Portlandia sketch where Fred and Carrie are getting ready to head to a friend’s birthday party, but Fred says they should try out a TV show he’s heard great things about. Carrie reluctantly agrees to try one episode before they leave, but then they have to go to the party. They’ll at least make it there for dessert, right? They do not.

More than two decades after Battlestar Galactica premiered, the show remains dangerously well-engineered for exactly this kind of behavior. And with the entire series streaming for free on Pluto TV, it's remarkably easy for anyone to become Fred and Carrie, or Corey and Kevin.

Battlestar Galactica radically reimagines the campy 1978 series of the same name. Humanity has created a race of artificial beings called Cylons, the robots have rebelled, and they've returned after decades of peace to wipe out the human race. A tiny fleet of survivors escapes under the protection of the aging Battlestar Galactica, led by Commander William Adama (Edward James Olmos), and sets off in search of the mythical planet Earth.
But Battlestar Galactica immediately reveals its best gimmick: Some Cylons look exactly like humans.
points: Moore’s beloved sci-fi series that ran for four seasons from 2004 to 2009.
Once Fred and Carrie start watching, they cannot stop.

articles.title: Anya Taylor-Joy's Near-Perfect Breakout Folk Thriller Is Officially Leaving Netflix
articles.summary: Anya Taylor-Joy has firmly established herself as one of her generation’s leading and most versatile actors. At 30, she has built a career across film and television, appearing in franchises like Super Mario and Mad Max, and winning a Golden Globe for her role in The Queen’s Gambit.
body: The Witch premiered in 2015, serving as a calling card for Taylor-Joy as a rising star and Robert Eggers as a director to look out for. It also turned Black Phillip the goat into a contemporary horror icon almost overnight. More than a decade later, the film remains just as invigorating. It’s currently streaming on Netflix, but only until Oct. 1 — so you’ve got a matter of days left to watch it.

The Witch follows a devout, isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England, a time when witches, myth, and folklore quietly stood at the root of most people’s everyday fears. Following their exile from the religious community due to a dispute with the church, a family of seven is forced to relocate to the outskirts of society, with the dark, unmapped woods mere feet away.

The film is steeped in its historical setting, and its characters speak a dense form of archaic English, with religion at the very center of their lives. That can be a tough watch for modern viewers, but The Witch ultimately tells a simple story about a family hitting its breaking point.

articles.title: The Love Hypothesis Review
articles.summary: The Love Hypothesis review: Ali Hazelwood’s New York Times bestseller gets adapted into a charming rom-com.
body: Sometimes a rom-com isn’t just a rom-com; such is the case with The Love Hypothesis, a Prime Video movie adaptation of author Ali Hazelwood's 2021 New York Times bestseller. In most cases, that’s a cut-and-dry scenario. However, Hazelwood’s book evolved out of the author’s frustration with how the Star Wars sequels turned out; she, among many, was so frustrated with how the characters of Rey and Kylo Ren/Ben Solo were done dirty in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker that she “fixed” their outcomes through a creative outpouring of fan fiction. One of them was rewritten as The Love Hypothesis and published, turning into an international BookTok sensation and now a movie.

articles.title: Second wave of Xbox cuts reported to be happening this week, with "several" studios apparently facing consolidation
articles.summary: Xbox is reportedly preparing to lay off hundreds more people this week as the company plans to consolidate several of its studios.
body: The news comes from an exclusive report on The Information, which cites a source briefed about Microsoft's plans. The report does not say which of Xbox's many studios are affected and which are being consolidated.

If correct, this would be the second wave of Xbox layoffs this year, following major restructuring in July that resulted in 1,600 job cuts. This is part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's plan to "reset" Microsoft's gaming division and return it to profitability. When those cuts were announced, Sharma also said the company intended to cut a further 1,600 jobs before a year had passed (taking us to next summer, approximately). These reported layoffs could be that second wave.

July's layoffs saw cuts across almost the entirety of Xbox's studio portfolio, though some teams were more affected than others. Xbox also shed a handful of studios, with some of those, such as Double Fine Productions and Compulsion Games, buying back their independence. Other studios, such as Ninja Theory and State of Decay maker Undead Labs, were instead sold to as-yet unnamed buyers, and Dishonored studio Arkane Lyon is undergoing consultation, and its fate remains unknown.

articles.title: Stephen King's Most Unhinged Sci-Fi Action Masterpiece Is Officially Free to Watch on YouTube
articles.summary: Stephen King is one of the definitive authors of our time. Known as a horror master, he’s worked across all sorts of genres, from high fantasy to dystopian fiction. King's visions of the future are often just as bleak as his work in horror, swapping supernatural monsters for advanced technology and…
body: One of King's most prophetic books was released in 1982 under the pen name Richard Bachman. The Running Man has a Simpsons -esque knack for predicting our future: a world where spectacle is wielded to influence the public and keep them in line.

While Edgar Wright put a modern spin on King's story in 2025, there's still something charming and surprisingly resonant in the extremely campy version that came out in 1987 starring Arnold Schwarzenegger at the height of his action-star powers. That version of The Running Man is now free to stream on YouTube, and it takes the real and somber concerns of King’s novel to hilarious (and believable) extremes.

Directed by Paul Michael Glaser, The Running Man opens with a helpful crawl in bright white letters over a red backdrop, laying out the vision of the future while establishing the film’s striking color palette.

articles.title: Here’s Why A Nightmare On Elm Street Game Hasn’t Happened In Decades
articles.summary: With Friday the 13th, Halloween, and other horror franchises getting video game adaptations in recent years, you might wonder when it'll be Freddy Krueger's turn, but according to Illfonic, the team behind those games, the task is harder than you might think.
body: With Freddy's dream world seeming like a great fit for a game, I'd long envisioned Elm Street as an obvious candidate for an asymmetrical multiplayer horror game akin to Illfonic's other titles, but listening to Gerritzen speak on the pitfalls, it occurred to me that he's right.

It's hard to imagine a game creating enough elaborate set-piece kills to keep them feeling fresh for players who may play for dozens or hundreds of hours, but neither does it make sense to rinse and repeat the same standout moments like Tina's nightmare that saw her crawling on the ceiling, or the way Glen's bed swallows him whole and erupts with a geyser of blood.

Freddy doesn't usually catch up to someone and finish them off with his iconic glove in a way that maps well onto multiplayer. He makes a meal out of them, and that's hard to translate into a game built on replayability.
Gerritzen explained that his team has worked on so many games of this sort that, by now, it gives them something like a running start.

articles.title: Comparing Games Like Halloween To Dead By Daylight Doesn’t Make Sense, Illfonic Says
articles.summary: Halloween is the latest in a long line of asymmetrical multiplayer horror games to release over the past decade, and like all the others, it's faced lots of comparisons to Dead by Daylight (DBD), the decade-long leader in the genre.
body: "It's literally cricket versus baseball. It's so easy to see an image of cricket and say it's exactly like baseball; it's like, really, is it? No, it's not. Like, here are all these differences," Gerritzen told me in a Zoom call. Illfonic is no stranger to this space, having made Friday the 13th, Predator: Hunting Grounds, Ghostbusters: Spirits Unleashed, and Killer Klowns from Outer Space all before Halloween.
"We make a game bespoke for that franchise, for that group of horror fans, and for the people who love that monster."
Gerritzen said that "others" make something more like "mixtapes," which have their own merits, but the projects are too different to directly compare, as some players do.

"And it's like, how could you not want something that is built purely for Halloween? Like, if you're a horror fan, if you're a Halloween fan, how would you just be okay with it being a secondary piece? We build things for that love of that movie, and I feel like they deserve it.

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Reacts To People Who Didn’t Like The Controversial Ending, Says It Was Almost Completely Different
articles.summary: The new Resident Evil movie from director Zach Cregger hit theaters on September 18, and it had a scary-good first weekend at the box office. The movie got great reviews but some people didn't like the ending specifically.
body: Cregger said in new interviews that he respects that, but doesn't agree--and the ending was almost totally different.

The Resident Evil movie ends by revealing that Austin Abrams' character, Bryan, becomes an infected demon after getting bitten by a child, and that the movie is actually the origin story of a monster that you might find in the games. The syringe carrying the cure to the virus shatters on the ground. In the original version, Cregger said the syringe with the cure also broke, but at that moment, Bryan simply went on a killing spree.

However, test screenings resulted in negative feedback, with people saying this was deflating and meant that the story was "over." However, Cregger told Collider that he filmed a second sequence as a Plan B, and that's the one that ended up in the movie where people root for Bryan to be cured. It led to a greater emotional journey for viewers, Cregger said, though not everyone agrees.
In a separate interview with The New Flesh Horror Movie Podcast, Cregger said he liked the idea of Bryan reaching his "final form" as a mutant monster, especially because it's not what you'd expect.

articles.title: Pokémon Winds and Winds Leaks Tease A Pokédex Too Massive To Finish
articles.summary: This summer's Pokémon Winds and Waves rumors and leaks suggested next year’s mainline entry could feature 300 new Pokémon. These leaks, by any rational person’s read, should be taken with an entire Stantler lick of salt. But they’re nevertheless worrying.
body: Fans are pretty split on whether 300 new Pokémon is a thrilling prospect of creature-collecting or an absurdly wild swing that would oversaturate an already pretty saturated compendium of monsters. One caveat, according to the leaks, is that Winds and Waves won’t literally add 300 entirely new Pokémon; that number could comprise alternate forms or regional variants in addition to wholly original Pokémon.

And this isn’t just nostalgia talking. In the Pokémon community, there’s a meme-ified refrain that “every Pokémon is someone’s favorite.” In 2025, one YouTuber actually put that notion to the test in a wide-ranging survey of more than 26,000 respondents. More than 50 Pokémon didn’t get any votes at all. Of those, just one of the original 151. (Pour one out for poor Tentacool.) Meanwhile, the most-beloved Pokémon largely originated in earlier generations.

videos.summary: Play Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, now on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch:
body: Armed with Joshua's harmonica and an unshakable determination, Estelle embarks upon a continent-spanning quest to find her partner.

During her journey, she must take on the sinister society of Ouroboros as it emerges from the shadows to plunge Liberl into utter chaos. Confronted with the greatest crisis in the history of the kingdom, Estelle and her allies battle to find Joshua and untangle the web of intrigue and conspiracy woven by Ouroboros!
